links.reason: Both are veri complaints: K263 வேற்றுப் பெருந் தெய்வம் ... பேஎய்க் கொளீஇயள் இவளெனப் படுதல் நோதக்கன்றே, A292 வேலன் ... தூங்கும் ஆயின், அதூஉம் நாணுவல். The split between the girl's shame (நாணுவல்) and the friend's protest at a false verdict is real, but it is the stock veri situation seen by two speakers, and 'develops' overstates a side-by-side.

The Kural presupposes the heart that goes out (யாருழைச் சேறி) and rebukes it, so it does not contradict Kainnilai's என்நெஞ்சு நீந்து நெடுவிடைச் சென்று; the two agree the heart leaves and the Kural adds that the going is needless. Teaches calls the Kainnilai 'the older picture', but this minor-canon venba is no older than the Kural.

Both open உள்ளார் கொல்லோ தோழி and close on the men who crossed (சுரன் இறந்தோரே / காடிறந் தாரே), and each fills the middle with a male creature tending its mate: பல்லி தன்றுணை பயிரும் against the களிறு that wards off bowmen so the பிடி and calf drink (வில் கடிந்து ஊட்டின பெயரும்). The contrast between a call and an act of provision is in the Tamil; that it mirrors his going to provide is inference but fair.

The shared figure is real: Paripadal's கடும் புனல் கை வாங்க, நெஞ்சம் அவள் வாங்க and Kalittokai's புதுப் புனல் நின்னைக் கொண்டு ஈர்த்து உய்ப்பக் கண்டார் உளர், both at Vaigai bathing. But the claim that the Kalittokai's irony 'depends on the audience knowing the Paripadal scene' is unsupported; the woman-as-flood mapping (அறல், கயல்) stands on its own.

Ainkurunuru 492 likens peacock, mullai and deer to her (நின்னே போலும் மஞ்ஞை) as the man returns; Kar Narpathu 9's flowers bloom கண்மலர்போல் and 'announce' his coming (வரல்கூறும்). Season signs likened to the woman and pointing to return are the common mullai stock; teaches restates that in grander words ('the bond that carries the promise across'), and உருவினை in KN9 line 1 is unclear.

The specific charge matches: Ainkurunuru 41 தன்சொல் உணர்ந்தோர் மேனி பொன்போல் செய்யும் and Akananuru 146 மாயப் பரத்தன் வாய்மொழி நம்பி ... கண் பசந்து, both pallor from trusting his word. The shift from a general habit (plural உணர்ந்தோர்) to a forecast for the next woman, framed by எம்போல், is in the Tamil.
links.text_issue: akananuru:146 line 8 அனியள் is likely a misprint for அளியள்.

links.reason: Both do use the Sur killing and the thunangai: Perumpanatruppadai's கடுஞ்சூர்க் கொன்ற பைம்பூட் சேஎய் பயந்த ... துணங்கையஞ் செல்வி, and the பேய்மகள் who dances துணங்கை in Thirumurugatruppadai. But in Perumpanatruppadai the bard's praise is likened to spirits snapping fingers before the goddess, Murugan's mother, not to praise of Murugan. And the demoness's battlefield dance is not 'the form of Murugan's praise', so teaches misdescribes what was lent.

ஏற்பாரைப் பார்த்து உவக்கும் is the givers' city rejoicing to have receivers. That is the giver's joy, which the Kural itself values, and it does not call taking (கொளல்) good. The 'opposite views of asking' need a reading the line does not force; the fragment's ranking of Koodal over புத்தேள் உலகு is also unlike the Kural's மேலுலகம் இல்லெனினும் hypothetical.

The shared pun is real and the same poet: நாள்வேங்கை (kino) beside கோள்வேங்கை (tiger) in both, the tiger being the brothers and mother in 20 (கோள்வேங்கை போற்கொடியார் என்ஐயன்மார்) and the lover in 31 (கோள்வேங்கை யன்னான்). Nothing makes 31 the friend 'pressing the girl toward him'; she puzzles over his reserve (எவன்கொலோ ... குறிப்பு), and 31's tiger is praise, not danger, so the staged narrative in teaches is imposed.

Song 8 says பரங்குன்று இமயக் குன்றம் நிகர்க்கும் because of the god, and song 18 says இக் குன்று ... ஏறுமாறு ஏற்கும் against நின் சீர் நிரந்து ஏந்திய குன்று. The contrast of settled equality and accepted contest is fair. But song 18 never names the rival hill as the Himalaya, so the pairing leans on an identification the words leave open.

உப்பு in both is real: உப்பாதல் சான்றோர் கடன் for friendship's liberties (கெழுதகைமை) and உப்பமைந் தற்றால் புலவி. But in 802 salt is the relish the worthy add, while in 1302 it is a dose that spoils when exceeded. That 1302 'supplies the measure 802 leaves out' transfers the love couplet's warning into friendship, which neither verse does.

Verse 3 credits honours and rain at command to the பத்தினி; verse 4 says கள்அவிழ் கோதையர் ... காமனொடு ஆயினும் உள்ளம் பிறிதாய் உருகலும். Both are fragments with unknown speakers, and praise of the rare chaste wife is compatible with a general charge of fickleness, so the clash is limited. The teaches sentence states this dependence honestly.

The rare compound அடுநறா is shared, and the Kural's claim that brewed toddy delights only its drinker (உண்டார்கண் அல்லது) is met by a drunk dancer who is part of a scene the poet likens to a painting (ஓவத்து எழுது எழில்). The link turns on one word, though, and the painting is of three women's moods, not of the toddy, so the pairing needs a generous reading.

Kuttuvan's western land is named in both: Akananuru 91 குட்டுவன் காப்ப ... குடநாடு பெறினும் தவிரலர், and Natrinai 105 குட்டுவன் குட வரைச் சுனைய ... குவளை ... கமழும் அம் சில் ஓதி. The friend's outside assurance that his land would not hold him, set against the man's own heart turning back to her hair scented like that land's lilies, is a specific use of the puram name.

The Kural ties rain to the king's justice (முறைகோடி ... ஒல்லாது வானம் பெயல்). Kalittokai 99 grants exactly that, மழை சுரந்து ... பிழையாது வருதல் நின் செம்மையின் தர. It then asks whether she fell outside the parasol, sceptre and drum (புற நிழல் கீழ்ப் பட்டாளோ இவள்?), so the doctrine's public test is met while the wife is wronged.

The sea-scooping cloud (கடல்முகந்து கார் / கடனீர் முகந்த ... எழிலி) is a stock image of the rains, and Kainnilai 34 is mostly lacuna. Making one poet's appointed sign and the other poet's arrival 'close the loop' is a shared stock phrase dressed up as a sequence.
links.text_issue: kainnilai:34 lines 1, 2 and 4 are largely lost.

links.reason: Akananuru 242 says the mother does not know (அறியாள்) that the one who chased parrots with them (செந்தார்க் கிள்ளை நம்மொடு கடிந்தோன்) came in love, and brings the அறியா வேலன். Natrinai 288 has the friend fear the verdict சிறு கிளி கடிகம் சென்றும் ... நெடு வேள் அணங்கிற்று. The point that the rite finds the right place and names the wrong agent is in the Tamil.

The quoted order matches: Akananuru 74 'திண்தேர் வலவ! கடவு' inside the friend's comfort, and Ainkurunuru 488 கடவுமதி தேரே as the rains begin (பெயல் தொடங்கின்றே). That is accurate, but the man's order to the charioteer at the rains is the stock mullai return, a whole decade's theme, so the pairing adds little beyond the shared situation.

Both have the ageing wife speak to the bard: மூத்தேம் ... நீத்தல் அறிந்திலேம் in 45 and தளர் முலையாய் மூத்தமைந்தார் உத்தரம் வேண்டா வரல் in 48. The move from belated insight to refusal is plausible, but 48's last line is obscure and பொலிவுடைத்தா is unclear, so the 'reason for closing the door' rests on an uncertain reading.

The balance image is shared and used for the same thing, judging without leaning: Kural 118 சமன்செய்து சீர்தூக்குங் கோல்போல் ... ஒருபால் கோடாமை, and Maduraikkanchi's court ஞெமன்கோ லன்ன செம்மைத்தாகி. The idyll states the condition as setting aside அச்சமும் அவலமும் ஆர்வமும், செற்றமும் உவகையும. That gives the couplet's 'first making level' a named content.

The formula is near verbatim: நீரினும் இனிய சாயல் (Pari) and வானி நீரினும் தீந்தண் சாயலன் (Poraiyan). Patitruppattu 86 sets it explicitly against the reputation of slaughter that frightened the poet (வெப்புடை ஆடூஉச் செத்தனென் மன்யான்), so the reuse does new work.

The shared symptom is the shoulders slipping with the bangles: வளையொடு சோரும் என் தோள் and பைந்தொடி சோரும் ... தோள். This is the commonest sign of separation in the corpus. The teaches sentence mainly restates that the venba adds a scene (கலையொடு மான்இரங்கும் ... அத்தம்), which any akam poem does.

The formula is verbatim: வரிநுணல் கறங்க ... கார்தொடங் கின்றே காலை in both. Ainkurunuru 468 runs on to வருவர் இன்றுநம் காதலோரே, and Akananuru 364 to a man who does not think of them and an evening hard to swim through (நீந்தலோ அரிதே). So the same opening hinges to opposite outcomes.
links.text_issue: ainkurunuru:468 line 4 is supplied from another source.

links.reason: The image is distinctive and shared: பொதியிற் கடவுள் போகிய கருந்தாட் கந்தத்து (A307) and கடவுள் கந்தம் கைவிடப் பலிகண் மாறிய பாழ்படு பொதியில் (P52). The akam poet's turn, the dove that will not leave from long dwelling (உடனுறை பழமையின் துறத்தல் செல்லாது), set against the man who will leave, is in the Tamil.

The two speeches are rival women's taunts from opposite sides: the parattai calls him the wife's ஆடிப் பாவை, and the wife counts rivals வண்டினும் பலரே. They are not incompatible claims about one thing. And the wife in Ainkurunuru 67 does not say the other woman has no power over him, only that she is one of many.

Kural 1168 says the night has none but her for company (என்னல்லது இல்லை துணை). Kuruntokai 86 asks பிறருங் கேட்குநர் உளர்கொல் and finds only the bell that rings each time the lonely cow stirs (ஆனுளம் புலம்புதொறு). The shared புலம்பு makes the cow her one fellow-waker, a specific answer to the Kural's claim.

இன்னே வருகுவர் occurs in both, followed by the weeping refusal: காட்டவுங் காட்டவுங் காணாள் கலுழ்சிறந்து and உகத்தவை மொழியவும் ஒல்லாள் மிகக்கலுழ்ந்து. The note's first clause is loose, since in Mullaippattu the words are the herd-girl's to the calf, not said to the wife, but teaches states that difference correctly, omen against the nurses' comfort.

Ainkurunuru 394 does reverse a verdict: அன்பில் அறனும் அருளிற்று மன்ற. But 376 curses பால், fate (அறனில் பாலே), not அறம. The note merges the two words, so the reversal is of the household's earlier complaint inside 394 rather than of 376's curse.

The opening formula அன்னாய் வாழி வேண்டு அன்னை with பசந்தனள் is genuinely shared. But Akananuru 48 is the colophon's அறத்தொடு நிற்றல, a told story, while Ainkurunuru 366 is an evasive answer in a paalai decade (கோங்கம் பயந்த மாறே). Calling the kongu line 'the same disclosure compressed' needs a generous reading.

The five are the same list (சுவைமை, இசைமை, தோற்றம், நாற்றம், ஊறு against சுவைஒளி ஊறுஓசை நாற்றம்): the Kural places the world in the grasp of the one who discerns them (வகைதெரிவான் கட்டே உலகு), and the hymn says அவையும் நீயே. Neither limits the other. The same list serving mastery and worship is a parallel across domains, and 'withdrawal' reads in the chapter context more than the couplet.

Both set one sleepless woman against a sleeping world: துஞ்சும் ஊர்க்கே and மன்னுயிர் எல்லாம் துயிற்றி. The contrast between rage (மூட்டுவேன்கொல் தாக்குவேன்கொல்) and the Kural's address to the night is real, but it is the shared topic of the lone sleepless lover told in two tones.

Both are the man arguing with a heart bent on wealth, and both use the desert's killers. But Akananuru 327's killers grieve only when the arrow misses (கொன்றோர் கோல்கழிபு இரங்கும்), which says nothing about what the victim carries. Only 337's Mazhavar kill for possible gold (பொன்னா குதலும் உண்டு), so 'weighing a life by what he might carry' fits one poem only.

The words line up: Akananuru 1 பிரியலம் என்ற சொல்தாம் மறந்தனர் கொல்லோ rests the betrayal on a spoken vow, and Ainkurunuru 336 பிரியலர் போலப் புணர்ந்தோர் rests it on the embrace. Both men have gone for wealth (பொலங்கல வெறுக்கை / பொருட்பிணி), and the contrast of word and embrace is specific.

The otter line is verbatim: நீர்நாய் வாளை நாளிரை பெறூஉம் ஊர(ன்). The note is right that the speakers are the wife and the இற்பரத்தை. But in both the line is only the husband's town-epithet, and neither poem bends it to the speaker's side, so 'each woman fits it to her side of the quarrel' is not shown.

The Kural makes slipping bangles the gossip of separation (தூற்றாகொல் ... இறைஇறவா நின்ற வளை). Natrinai 136's father fits போக்கு இல் பொலந் தொடி that தோள் பழி மறைக்கும், and the physician simile (அறவோன் போல) marks it as a treatment of the sign, not the sickness. The qualification is in the Tamil.

Kazhuvul is named in both: ஆன்பயம் வாழ்நர் கழுவுள் தலைமடங்க under the Chera, and ஈர்எழு வேளிர் இயைந்துஒருங்கு எறிந்த கழுவுள் காமூர் போலக் கலங்கின்று ... என் நெஞ்சே. The note says what the akam poet does with the name: the trusting heart is a besieged fort.

Kar Narpathu 4 makes the konrai season பசலை மருந்து. Kuruntokai 148 answers a friend who now denies the season (காரன் றென்றி யாயின் கனவோ மற்றிது), with konrai and kurundham in bloom. The reversal of the friend's seasonal argument once the date has passed is in both texts.

The bard-as-witness instruction is shared: காண்மதி பாணநீ யுரைத்தற் குரியை and கண்டாங்கு உரையாய் கொண்மோ பாண. But a single three-line poem is not a 'convention', and nothing shows Natrinai 291 expanding it by borrowing from war poetry; the Mullur raid simile is simply this poem's own figure.

The contrast in these two passages is real: நின் வெம்மையும் விளக்கமும் ஞாயிற்று உள ... நிற் பிரிந்து against தானே ... ஞாயிறும் திங்களும். But the historical claim that identity was later is false within the Paripadal itself: song 13 says விசும்பும் நீயே, வளியும் நீயே, and so the Sangam hymns already make the god the elements.
links.text_issue: Paripadal 4 line 25 is flagged as a possible dropped heading.

links.reason: The clause is verbatim: நீர் இன்று அமையா உலகம் போல and நீர்இன்று அமையாது உலகெனின். It is a premise in Valluvar's argument for rain and a simile of dependence in Kapilar (தம் இன்று அமையா நம்), which supports the reading of a shared saying put to two uses.

Same poet and same kandor voice. Kuruntokai 7 pities both (நல்லோர் யார்கொல் அளியர்), while Natrinai 2 judges the youth: இளையோன் உள்ளம் ... உருமினும் கொடிதே. That the onlookers can move from pity to blame of the hero is shown by the two texts.

The seven givers and the stock epithets are shared: Pekan's அருந்திறல் அணங்கின் / அருந்திறல் கடவுள் காக்கும் with பெருங்கல் நாடன், and the closing என ஆங்கு எழுவர். Puram 158 says எழுவர் மாய்ந்த பின்றை and summons Kumanan, while the idyll ends on எழுவர் பூண்ட ஈகைச் செந்நுகம், the yoke its patron takes up. The two uses of the canon differ as teaches says.

The link to புலவியும் வீழுநர் கண்ணே இனிது is real: a pulavi needs love on both sides. But ஊரன் புலக்கும் தகையமோ can mean 'am I still fit to sulk at him' as well as 'would he quarrel with me', and teaches depends on the second reading.

iraicchi.act: the stag embraces its doe and shelters with her in the bush at evening
iraicchi.sense: even the stag keeps its mate close at nightfall, while he who spoiled her beauty has not come

poems.note: Two creature pairs (stag and doe, tusker and she-elephant) act alike; the first was taken as the carrier.

iraicchi.act: having caught a prawn, it searches the backwater and calls to the mate it loves
iraicchi.sense: the shore's male bird provides for and calls its mate, while the lord delays marrying her

poems.note: The crab's hole filled with falling paddy flowers invites a reading of the husband, but neither poem nor colophon thurai states his straying.
The poem states the moral itself (காமம் ... உணரார் மாட்டும் சென்றே நிற்கும்).
The bat flying off marks the evening; no clear implication for the lovers.
Fragment: most lines are lost, so the situation the stag-and-doe pair would point to cannot be checked.
The season images are all open similes (மடி இலான் செல்வம் போல், மாயவள் மேனி போல்).
The heron is addressed throughout, so striking its lines removes the poem.

iraicchi.act: the boar guards its young against the tigress's striped cub
iraicchi.sense: even the boar protects its own, while the hill lord forgot and left her with their son

iraicchi.act: the crab plays with its mate
iraicchi.sense: creatures of the shore stay and play with their mates, while he has gone away

poems.note: The venba's syntax is compressed; the crab pair is set beside the man who left.

iraicchi.act: the stag, having drunk clear water, frolics with its beloved mate
iraicchi.sense: the paired deer rejoice together in the rains, while the man who should have come stays away

poems.note: The falling mullai petals are joined directly to her tears (இதழழிந்து ஊறும் கண்பனி).
The crow hanging sleepless in the rain, longing for offerings, matches her wakefulness, but only one correspondence is firm.
The crab-and-prawn scene is tied to her brow by the open comparison அற்றே.

iraicchi.act: the birds, having mated, call sweetly from the branch
iraicchi.sense: the paired birds' union sharpens her grievance at the absent man she means to rebuff

poems.note: The whole poem turns on the 'foolish' cloud, so its lines cannot be struck.
